items.title: Legal Specialist, Law Enforcement
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We are looking for a hands-on Legal Specialist (Law Enforcement) to join our Litigation, Regulatory & Policy team at Anthropic. In this role, you will be a key player in building out our legal function and running how Anthropic responds to law enforcement and government requests for user data, while navigating the intricate regulatory landscape of the AI industry. We expect this role to flex beyond the law enforcement queue into legal operations to support the broader litigation, regulatory, and policy team. The successful candidate will be a strong team player, able to build positive relationships with colleagues and work collaboratively toward shared goals. Key responsibilities Own the end-to-end response to law enforcement and government requests for user data, from intake and validation through production and closeout, including subpoenas, court orders, search warrants, preservation letters, and emergency disclosure requests from domestic and foreign authorities Prepare and execute data productions: scoping, data retrieval, coordination with counsel, and eventual production Handle foreign and cross-border process, including MLATs and letters rogatory, and manage escalations across jurisdictions Handle civil third-party subpoenas and preservation demands Maintain expertise in where user data lives across Anthropic's product surfaces and operate the internal data retrieval tooling Run and improve the law enforcement response process and tooling Partner with Trust and Safety, Security, Privacy, and Engineering on requests that touch user accounts, investigations, or safety escalations Coordinate with outside counsel, alongside in-house counsel, on objections, challenges, and narrowing Produce recurring reporting on request volume, deadlines, and queue health, and support Anthropic's periodic transparency reporting on government requests Monitor legal developments in government access to user data and advise the team on their operational impact Support litigation and regulatory matters and stretch beyond core responsibilities as needed to support the legal team's objectives Minimum qualifications Experience in a legal operations, business/operations manager, or paralegal role in an in-house legal department, or similar experience Direct, front-line experience handling law enforcement or government requests for user data, including subpoenas, court orders, warrants, preservation letters, and emergency disclosure requests Working knowledge of the legal framework for law enforcement access to user data, including the Stored Communications Act and the mechanics of foreign and cross-border requests such as MLATs Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with colleagues at all levels of the organization Demonstrated ability to exercise good judgment and maintain the highest standards of discretion and confidentiality when handling sensitive legal matters, including under time pressure Strong project management skills, including the ability to prioritize tasks, meet deadlines, and manage multiple projects simultaneously Experience owning an intake, queue, or docketing process end to end, including deciding what gets escalated and maintaining rigorous tracking Comfort operating and improving the tooling a legal process runs on (trackers, spreadsheets, forms, aliases, and simple automations), with a willingness to make changes directly rather than route every change to someone else A proactive, solutions-oriented approach to identifying, recommending, and implementing process improvements within the legal department Preferred qualifications 5+ years of experience in legal operations, business/operations management, or a paralegal role in an in-house legal department 2+ years of experience at a high-growth technology company, with exposure to the legal challenges and opportunities presented by emerging technologies Experience building or scaling a law enforcement response process Experience managing legal intake process within a growing company Demonstrated ability to think critically and creatively, adapting to new challenges and finding practical solutions to complex legal issues Familiarity with legal project management software such as Asana, Trello, or Jira, and a willingness to learn and adopt new tools to streamline legal processes The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $170,000 — $220,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.title: Trust & Safety Ads Operations Analyst, Data
items.description: About the Team At OpenAI, Trust & Safety Operations is central to protecting OpenAI’s platform, customers, and the public from abuse. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, Legal, Policy and Go To Market teams to identify emerging risks, build and mature enforcement systems, and ensure high-integrity operations while delivering a great user experience at scale. We’re building the Monetization Trust & Safety Operations team to ensure OpenAI can grow advertising in a way that is safe, trusted, and sustainable—for users, advertisers, and the business. This team sits at the intersection of operational scale, product risk, and rapid revenue growth, designing systems and operations that enable ads to scale without compromising user trust or safety. It’s critical to us that our Ads product be built in a way that corresponds to our Ads principles https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fopenai%2Ecom%2Findex%2Four-approach-to-advertising-and-expanding-access%2F&urlhash=tnG4&isSdui=true, and this team is key to that. About the Role We’re looking for a senior operator with strong analytical instincts to help build and scale Monetization Trust & Safety Operations at OpenAI. In this role, you’ll flex across the team’s highest-priority data and operational needs—from reporting and dashboard insights to budget and capacity planning, project-based analysis, and data automation —while partnering closely with Product, Policy, Engineering, Legal, Go To Market, and Data Science and Data Engineering teams. This role sits at the intersection of strategy, execution, and data: you’ll define ambiguous problems, query and validate data, build decision-support systems, and translate operational signals into clear recommendations and scalable, AI-first solutions. You should be comfortable moving from a high-level question to a rigorous analysis, a useful dashboard, an automated workflow, or a durable operating mechanism. As OpenAI introduces new revenue-generating formats and partnerships, you’ll help the team understand where risks, capacity constraints, quality gaps, and opportunities are emerging. You’ll bring structure to ambiguity and ensure Ads Trust & Safety decisions are grounded in reliable data while balancing user safety, advertiser experience, and business growth. In this role, you will: - Own complex, high-impact Ads Trust & Safety data and operational problem areas from scoping through execution. - Improve recurring reporting and dashboards by defining meaningful metrics, surfacing trends and gaps, and translating insights into operational decisions. - Lead budget and capacity planning by connecting demand, review volumes, service levels, quality, and risk signals to staffing and operating plans. - Conduct project-based analyses across advertiser risk, enforcement performance, review quality, product launches, and operational health; turn findings into clear recommendations and next steps. - Partner closely with Data Science and Data Engineering teams to define goals, metric logic, data requirements, source-of-truth decisions, and QA data strategy. - Design and maintain practical data-quality and measurement mechanisms, including sampling, validation, discrepancy investigation, quality dashboards, and feedback loops. - Build and improve automations, AI-assisted workflows, and decision-support tools that reduce manual work and help Ads Trust & Safety and Ads Support scale. - Drive operational readiness for new Ads and monetization launches, features, and markets by sizing impact, identifying risks early, and defining monitoring plans. - Act as a senior cross-functional partner and subject-matter expert, communicating data-driven tradeoffs, priorities, and recommendations with strong judgment and credibility. You might thrive in this role if you: - 8+ years of experience in Trust & Safety, Business Integrity, technical operations, data analytics, or a closely related domain. - Strong SQL skills and comfort working with unfamiliar, complex datasets, reconciling source-of-truth questions, and resolving data-quality issues. - Experience building and owning dashboards, recurring reporting, monitoring, or operational measurement systems from scoping through adoption and maintenance. - Experience using data for budget, capacity, or workforce planning, including translating demand, quality, and service-level signals into practical operating plans. - Proven ability to independently own ambiguous, cross-functional initiatives and turn analysis into decisions, workflows, or scalable systems. - In-depth experience leveraging AI models or agent-based tooling in operational workflows, or other lightweight technical development where useful. - Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex analyses, data limitations, risk tradeoffs, and recommendations to diverse audiences. - Strong judgment around quality, safeguards, responsible deployment, and the appropriate use of data in high-stakes operational decisions. - Bonus: Familiarity with ads and advertiser ecosystems and the operational signals that shape review, enforcement, and support decisions. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf. Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. To notify OpenAI that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form https://form.asana.com/?d=57018692298241&k=5MqR40fZd7jlxVUh5J-UeA. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this link https://form.asana.com/?k=bQ7w9h3iexRlicUdWRiwvg&d=57018692298241. items.title: Product Marketing Manager, Advertising & Engagement
items.location_text: New York, New York, United States
items.description: By bringing together next-gen technology and the finest live data available, Genius Sports is enabling a new era of sports for fans worldwide, delivering experiences that are more immersive, interactive and personalised than ever before. Learn more at geniussports.com About this role - Product Marketing Manager, Advertising & Engagement Genius Sports is evolving from a technology and services business into a more product-led organization. Within Advertising & Engagement, that means helping the market understand the breadth and value of our advertising portfolio — from official live data and fan identity to real-time activation products like Genius Sports Moments. This is one of the fastest-moving parts of our business: our Moment Engine now integrates with partners representing roughly 90% of the programmatic advertising ecosystem, and adoption is accelerating around tentpole moments like the Super Bowl, the NBA Finals and the FIFA World Cup. We are looking for a Product Marketing Manager, Advertising & Engagement to help shape, launch and grow our advertising technology portfolio. This is a high-impact role within one of Genius Sports' most strategically important and fastest-growing business areas, working closely with Product, Marketing, Commercial and Revenue teams to bring complex advertising products to market in a clear, compelling and commercially effective way. This role is ideal for a B2B product marketer who enjoys turning complex technology into sharp positioning, clear sales narratives and practical go-to-market plans. You will support the Advertising & Engagement marketing leadership while owning important workstreams across product launches, sales enablement, customer insight, product adoption and market positioning. You will play a central role in helping Genius Sports tell a stronger Advertising & Engagement story: not just as a trusted provider of official sports data, but as the execution layer connecting live sports data directly to real-time advertising activation — helping brands, agencies, broadcasters and platforms move from scheduled campaigns to always-on, moment-driven advertising. Responsibilities Product positioning and messaging Develop clear, differentiated positioning and messaging for Genius Sports' Advertising & Engagement products, translating technical capabilities into customer-centric value propositions. Build messaging frameworks that help Product, Commercial and Marketing teams consistently explain what our products do, who they are for, why they matter and how they compare in market. Help sharpen Genius Sports' advertising narrative around real-time activation, official data, fan identity and AI-powered decisioning — shifting the category conversation from scheduled media to moment-driven engagement. Go-to-market planning and product launches Own and support GTM plans for key Advertising & Engagement product launches, releases and strategic packages, including new capabilities, integrations and partnerships. Work with Product, Commercial and Marketing teams to define target audiences, customer pain points, launch objectives, timelines, KPIs, sales motions, collateral needs and campaign requirements. Sequence launches and campaigns against the global sports calendar, supporting major product and market moments including tentpole events like the Super Bowl, NBA Finals and FIFA World Cup, new season activity, and flagship industry events such as NewFronts. Sales enablement and commercial support Create foundational sales enablement materials that help Commercial teams confidently sell complex advertising and engagement products. Work with our Sales Marketing team to build sales decks, one-pagers, battlecards, product narratives, FAQs, internal briefings and training materials for audiences including brands, agencies, broadcasters, SSPs and demand platforms. Run product training and enablement sessions for Commercial teams, ensuring sales teams understand new products, releases, positioning and proof points. items.title: Reseller Enablement Lead
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the team Within GTM, the Partner Enablement team builds the programs, credentials, and learning infrastructure that allow Anthropic's ecosystem of system integrators, cloud providers, resellers, and technology partners to build deep Claude expertise and deliver successful customer outcomes at scale. We work cross-functionally across Partnerships, Sales, Applied AI, Product, Marketing, and Legal to make sure partner-facing programs are clear, consistent, and high-impact. About the role Anthropic is launching a global reseller program, and we are looking for a Reseller Enablement Lead to build the enablement motion that makes it work. You will design and launch reseller certification, training, and readiness programs alongside the program itself, starting in our first launch markets and scaling globally from there. This is a build-and-run role. In the first months you will stand up the foundation from scratch: what a reseller needs to know to sell Claude well, how we certify that they know it, and how we deliver that across markets and languages. From there, you will own the motion as it grows, evolving content and modalities as the program's commercial structure matures, localizing for new regions, and using enablement to keep partner behavior aligned with how we want Claude sold. You will be the single global owner for reseller enablement, scaling delivery through training networks rather than a large direct team. This is a highly cross-functional role working closely with Partnerships, Partner Programs, Partner Operations, Sales, Applied AI, and Certification to ensure reseller-facing programs land clearly and drive measurable outcomes. Responsibilities Define and own Anthropic's reseller enablement strategy, from launch in initial markets through global rollout Own delivery of the message you build: present and deliver training directly to reseller sellers and leaders, and activate training partners so they carry it consistently at scale Build the reseller curriculum and certification path from the ground up, covering commercial mechanics, program rules, platform and product fundamentals, and responsible use Design repeatable programs across partner onboarding, sales readiness, recertification, and product launches, choosing modalities that fit how reseller sellers actually learn and what motivates them Stand up localized delivery in launch markets, then extend the model to new regions through training networks and regional enablement teams Work closely with Applied AI to translate technical concepts into clear, digestible content on Anthropic's models and products for a seller audience Evolve enablement as the program evolves, keeping content current with changes to commercial structure, transaction rails, and program requirements Use enablement as a governance lever, building content and reinforcement that keeps partner selling behavior on program and addresses drift when it appears Enable Anthropic sellers and partner managers to co-sell and engage effectively with resellers Partner cross-functionally with Partner Programs, Partner Operations, and Sales to align priorities and ensure consistent execution Establish metrics and reporting to track reseller certification, activation, and contribution to registered pipeline and consumption Build feedback loops that bring reseller insights back into program design, enablement, and GTM strategy You may be a good fit if you Have 7-10+ years of experience across partner enablement, partner programs, product marketing, with a clear track record of designing and owning programs end to end. Channel and Alliances experience is key, but must be accompanied with demonstrated program ownership. Understand how resell and channel ecosystems work commercially, including deal registration, margin and rebate structures, partner tiering, and cloud marketplace motions Have built and scaled partner enablement or certification programs from nothing to something in a high-growth technology environment Think operationally and in systems, designing for scale across regions and languages rather than one-off efforts Understand how to package enablement: which modality fits which audience, what motivates partner sellers, and how to structure a curriculum that produces real selling capability Are a strong presenter and facilitator, able to deliver training credibly to partner audiences and equip others to deliver it the same way Combine leadership and hands-on execution, equally comfortable setting strategy with executives and building the first version of a course yourself Bring executive presence with partner and internal leadership, and the scrappiness to get things done in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment Are an effective cross-functional operator who can drive alignment across complex organizations Strong candidates may also have Experience launching programs in a single region and then scaling them globally, including localization and in-market delivery Experience building or running an authorized training partner or certified instructor network Prior ownership of, or close partnership with, a technology certification program Experience with resell motions in Japan, Korea, or other reseller-led markets A track record connecting enablement activity to pipeline and revenue outcomes Logistics This role is based in London. We operate a hybrid model and expect regular time onsite with partners and at Anthropic offices. Expect roughly 30-35% travel, concentrated around launch windows and launch regions. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: £160,000 — £215,000 GBP Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.title: Research Engineer - Web Crawlers
items.location_text: United Kingdom, United States, Poland, Bulgaria
items.description: ABOUT ELEVENLABS ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology. We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always. We have expanded from voice into three main platforms: - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale. - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages. - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models. Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you. HOW WE WORK - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy. - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you. - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations. - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models. - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location. WHAT WE OFFER - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities. - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend. - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose. - Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy. - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend. ABOUT THE ROLE We are looking for a Research Engineer to join the research team at ElevenLabs, focused on large-scale web crawling for our frontier AI models. The quality of our models is bounded by the quality and scale of the data behind them, and you will own the crawling systems that source world-class data from the open web. You will thrive in this role if you enjoy: - Building and operating large-scale, distributed web crawlers that discover, fetch, and extract data across billions of pages reliably and efficiently. - Solving hard crawling problems such as content extraction from messy HTML, deduplication at web scale, freshness and recrawl strategies, and politeness and rate-limit handling. - Designing targeted crawling pipelines that find high-value data sources, including audio, video, and multilingual content, and turn them into clean training-ready datasets. - Creating tooling and infrastructure that lets researchers request, monitor, and explore newly crawled web data quickly and reliably. REQUIREMENTS We do not require any formal certifications or degrees. Instead, we are seeking enthusiastic engineers who can showcase solving impressively hard problems with artifacts such as past projects, designs, or GitHub contributions. Ideally, you bring: - Hands-on experience building and scaling web crawlers or scraping systems, ideally in support of machine learning training data. - Strong engineering skills in distributed systems at scale (e.g., Kubernetes, queue-based architectures, or custom pipelines processing billions of documents). - The capacity to autonomously evaluate the quality, coverage, and compliance of crawled data, and to build the tooling to measure it. LOCATION This role is remote and can be executed globally. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in London, New York, San Francisco, and Warsaw. #LI-Remote We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We are seeking a Finance Business Partner to join our EMEA GTM Finance & Strategy team at Anthropic. In this role, you will be a key partner to our EMEA go-to-market teams, providing financial expertise and guidance to support strategic decision-making. As we continue to grow, you will play a crucial role in analyzing financial data, building models, and delivering insights to drive informed business decisions across revenue goals, sales capacity planning, deal desk and marketing spend returns. This role will work closely with cross-functional teams and collaborate with other members of the finance organization to align go-to-market strategies with broader financial considerations. Responsibilities: Provide expert guidance, recommendations, and influence to go-to-market stakeholders on financial strategies, investments, and resource allocation decisions, leveraging an in-depth understanding of the company's financials Partner cross-functionally to drive analysis, build financial models, and recommend business decisions across a variety of areas, such as revenue goals, sales capacity planning and key strategic initiatives Prepare and deliver clear, concise, and insightful financial reports, analyses, and forecasts, highlighting key trends, risks, and opportunities to facilitate informed decision-making to stakeholders and executives Collaborate with other members of strategic finance, FP&A, and accounting counterparts, helping to align go-to-market with broader financial strategies and considerations Requirements: 7+ years of experience across strategic finance, FP&A, business partnering, consulting, investment banking, or related fields Demonstrated experience supporting or building out finance functions in international or EMEA markets Exceptional analytical skills with the ability to synthesize complex data into clear, actionable insights and develop robust financial models Strong cross-functional communication skills and comfort presenting financial information to non-finance audiences, including senior leadership Experience with budgeting, forecasting, and long-range financial planning in a high-growth environment Familiarity with multi-entity, multi-currency financial environments and EMEA regulatory or statutory considerations A bias toward action, strong work ethic, and ability to drive outcomes under tight timelines Passion for Anthropic's mission to build safe, transformative AI systems The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: £240,000 — £240,000 GBP Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. items.title: Reseller Operations Manager, Japan & Korea
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic is expanding its reseller program in Japan and Korea. As our Reseller Operations Manager for Japan and Korea, you'll own how resellers in both countries get onboarded, transact, get paid, and get supported, across both of our resale motions: hyperscaler resale, where partners resell Claude through the cloud marketplaces (AWS Bedrock today, Google Cloud Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry to follow), and direct resale, where partners resell on Anthropic paper through our own quote-to-order and billing systems. The global team builds the program; you make it work for Japanese and Korean partners and feed back what has to change. This is an operator role, not a partner manager role. In the first months you'll be validating deal registrations and answering partner tickets yourself; by the end of the first year the volume should be running on documented process, service levels, and vendor or system coverage that you set up. Key responsibilities Own reseller onboarding for Japan and Korea end to end: application intake, screening coordination, agreement execution, marketplace authorization, entitlement setup, and activation, and keep the partner record in Salesforce decision-grade for both regions. Run hyperscaler (3P) reseller operations: deal-registration intake and validation within SLA, marketplace authorizations and private-offer processing with the cloud alliance teams, and end-customer reporting on every reseller transaction so partner-sourced revenue can be attributed. Run direct (1P) reseller operations: partner quotes and order forms, order booking and provisioning, and commit tracking and true-ups with Deal Desk, RevOps, and Accounting, and work with Finance and Tax on local invoicing, currency, and consumption-tax handling for each transaction route. Run the regional side of reseller incentives: eligibility, validation of quarterly payouts, and partner disputes, in partnership with the global incentive operations team and Finance. Stand up first-line operational support for resellers in Japanese and Korean during local business hours, inside the global partner support queue rather than alongside it, and localize the onboarding, deal-registration, and ordering content partners depend on. Manage any outsourced or contracted operations capacity used in region (scope, quality, service levels) and coordinate with Enablement on the logistics of local-language certification and training. Own reseller reporting for Japan and Korea: registration volume and cycle time, activation, attach, and attributed revenue by partner and by motion, and use it to tell the regional teams and the global program what to fix next. Adopt the global Partner Operations playbooks where they fit, write the in-region variants where they don't, and represent Japan and Korea requirements in partner systems and automation work so manual volume doesn't grow with partner count. Minimum qualifications Several years in channel, reseller, distribution, or partner operations at a technology company, ideally touching both a cloud-marketplace motion and a direct or contract-based resale motion. Working proficiency in Japanese, Korean, and English. We provide technical guidance, resolve complex issues and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our highly-capable models. We work closely with Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. We think from an automation-first mindset and leverage the latest in AI to scale our support operations. Join the Senior Support Engineering (SSE) team at OpenAI and help shape the future of Technical Support in the age of AI. About the Role We’re looking for a Support Engineering Manager to build and guide a high-performing team of experienced Senior Support Engineers with backgrounds in software engineering, site reliability engineering, and systems architecture. These engineers are trusted to operate with autonomy, tackle deeply technical challenges, and serve as the final escalation point before Engineering. In this role, you'll lead a team focused on deep problem-solving, proactive reliability work, and customer-specific troubleshooting. You’ll drive the design and operations of OpenAI’s incident management processes, including tooling, automations, and training, and ensure they are scalable and resilient. You’ll also oversee strategic customer workload monitoring, alerting, and a 24x7 rotation to ensure high-priority issues are caught early and handled with urgency. You’ll collaborate closely with Product, Engineering, Technical Success, and field teams to improve the supportability of our products, reduce operational burden, and shape the future of AI-driven technical support. Your team will own incident response playbooks, build internal automations, and serve as technical stewards for our most strategic accounts. This is an opportunity to define what world-class technical support looks like in the era of AGI. We're looking for a leader who combines strong technical depth with operational rigor, a passion for team development, and an automation-first mindset. The ideal candidate will have a combination of technical capabilities mixed with strong leadership and systems building strength. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. items.description: About the team OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. OpenAI for Government (OAI4G) helps public-sector institutions understand, adopt, and deploy highly capable AI products in support of their missions. The team brings together Sales, Solutions, Partnerships, Technical Success, Legal, Security, Policy, Global Affairs, and other cross-functional partners to help governments use AI responsibly and effectively. As part of OAI4G’s International Public Sector team, you will help public institutions in Australia and New Zealand (ANZ) and APAC translate frontier AI into secure, compliant, mission-aligned outcomes. We work across varied procurement, regulatory, security, sovereignty, and commercial environments, while maintaining a consistent commitment to safety, reliability, and public benefit. About the role We are seeking a senior Account Director (AD) to lead OpenAI’s public-sector work across ANZ, with a wider remit to develop selected priority opportunities across APAC. ANZ will be the centre of gravity for the role: you will build trusted relationships with government leaders, develop and execute account strategies, create and close complex opportunities, and help customers move from initial interest to successful adoption. This is a full-cycle, highly cross-functional sales role that combines technical understanding, strategic vision, partnership management, and value-driven execution. You will work with senior government, operational, technical, procurement, policy, and security stakeholders to identify high-impact AI use cases and translate them into credible commercial and deployment pathways across the OpenAI Platform API and Codex and ChatGPT Enterprise. You will also be an accountable customer leader after signature, working alongside specialist delivery and technical teams to keep customer outcomes, milestones, adoption, risks, and executive alignment on track. The role requires excellent judgement, executive presence, local fluency, and the ability to move between strategy, discovery, capture, procurement, delivery governance, and relationship management without day-to-day direction. This role can be based in Sydney (Hybrid model, 3 days in office) or remotely from Canberra. In this role, you will - Own a focused portfolio of ANZ public-sector accounts, while developing selected priority opportunities in APAC in line with OAI4G’s international strategy. - Build and execute comprehensive account plans that map mission priorities, stakeholders, procurement paths, partners, use cases, risks, and long-term expansion opportunities. - Drive complex opportunities through the full sales cycle, from pipeline generation, discovery, qualification, capture, and commercial strategy through negotiation, closure, adoption, and expansion. - Lead public-sector customers through their AI adoption journey, helping them identify responsible, high-impact use cases and connect mission outcomes to OpenAI’s capabilities and limitations. - Translate between government leaders, end users, technical teams, policy and security stakeholders, and internal product and engineering partners, clearly communicating requirements, progress, risks, and dependencies. - Serve as the accountable customer lead for engagements tied to clear outcomes, customer milestones, adoption measures, and commercial commitments, coordinating closely with technical specialists. - Work closely with the Partnerships team, global and regional system integrators, cloud and technology providers, local delivery partners, resellers, and strategic international partners to shape joint pursuits, deployment models, and purchasing paths. - Build trusted relationships with senior government executives and decision-makers, while staying close to operational users and technical stakeholders whose workflows determine successful adoption. - Maintain accurate pipeline, forecasting, account records, customer follow-up, and executive reporting, with disciplined follow-through across markets and time zones. - Monitor the government, technology, procurement, partner, and competitive landscape across ANZ and priority APAC markets, surfacing insights that inform product roadmaps and go-to-market strategy. - Represent OpenAI at government, partner, and industry forums, strengthening networks and identifying opportunities that advance responsible public-sector adoption of AI. We’re seeking someone with experience including - 10+ years in government, public-sector technology sales, business development, consulting, transformation, systems integration, or a closely related field, with meaningful ownership of complex customer outcomes. - Direct government experience or very significant experience working with government customers, ideally including sensitive agencies, national-security-adjacent environments, regulated missions, or high-consequence operational workflows. - A current Australian Government security clearance, with the ability to maintain the clearance required for the role. - Designing and executing complex deal strategies, including opportunity shaping before formal procurement, multi-stakeholder qualification, proposal development, negotiations, and closure. - Working directly with senior public-sector executives and decision-makers, alongside technical, operational, procurement, policy, and security stakeholders. - Navigating Australia’s public-sector procurement, contracting, security, privacy, data-residency, and compliance requirements; familiarity with New Zealand and/or other APAC public-sector environments is valuable. - Selling or delivering enterprise SaaS, cloud, AI/ML, data platforms, cybersecurity, API-based products, or other complex technology solutions in highly regulated environments. - Communicating technical, commercial, and strategic concepts clearly to both executive and working-level audiences, including the ability to explain where AI is and is not an appropriate fit. - Collaborating across Sales, Solutions, Partnerships, Research, Engineering, Technical Success, Legal, Security, Policy, Global Affairs, Finance, and Operations to move complex opportunities forward. - Operating with high ownership and sound judgement in ambiguous, fast-changing environments, while managing competing priorities across countries and time zones. - Travelling regularly within ANZ, and periodically across APAC, to work on-site with customers and partners. Nice to have - Deep relationships across Australian Commonwealth, state and territory, defence, national security, or other sensitive public-sector communities. - Experience building or working through local system-integrator, reseller, cloud-provider, or strategic-partner ecosystems. - Experience leading AI, digital, technology, or business-transformation initiatives from use-case shaping through deployment and adoption. - Familiarity with public-sector AI governance, responsible AI, cybersecurity, data sovereignty, and assurance requirements. - Experience developing opportunities across more than one APAC market and adapting to different political, cultural, regulatory, and procurement contexts. - Engineering, technical, policy, or operational experience that helps you translate complex AI capabilities into credible public-sector outcomes. You will thrive in this role if you - Are customer-centric. You work to understand public institutions’ missions and constraints deeply, and help them achieve meaningful outcomes with AI. - Are a strategist. You think years ahead, balance ANZ priorities with a broader APAC perspective, and align internal and external stakeholders around a clear point of view. - Are a builder. You create repeatable account, partner, capture, and delivery practices that can scale while adapting to local requirements. - Have strong judgement. You can navigate sensitive environments, incomplete information, competing priorities, and responsible-use considerations with integrity and composure. - Are technically curious. You can learn quickly, engage credibly with specialists, and translate frontier AI capabilities, limitations, and trade-offs for government audiences. - Care about public mission impact. items.description: About the Team OpenAI’s User Operations team ensures that our customers' experience is nothing short of exceptional. We resolve complex issues, provide guidance, and support customers in maximizing value with our products. Within User Operations, Ads Safety Operations helps OpenAI grow advertising in a way that is safe, trusted, and sustainable for advertisers, users and the business. The Ads Safety Support team sits within Ads Safety Operations and owns the advertiser-facing support journey: helping advertisers navigate ads products, policies, reviews, and enforcement decisions while turning frontline insights into better guidance, tooling, and product experiences. About the Role We’re looking for an Advertiser Support Specialist to help build and scale advertiser support within Ads Safety Operations. You’ll work directly with advertisers through support tickets, escalations, owning high-impact questions related to ads policies, review outcomes, product behavior, and operational processes. Many cases will be novel or ambiguous, and you’ll be expected to investigate carefully, communicate clearly, and drive them to resolution in a fast-moving product environment. As OpenAI’s advertising ecosystem grows, your work will help advertisers operate successfully at scale while serving as a critical bridge between frontline support and the teams responsible for product quality, policy integrity, and platform safety. Beyond resolving individual cases, you’ll help define what world-class support looks like in an AI-native environment. You’ll turn support interactions into operational intelligence, identifying recurring friction, gaps in guidance, and emerging issues to improve support at scale, and protect the quality and safety of OpenAI’s ad ecosystem. You’ll partner closely with Engineering, Product, Policy, Legal and Go To Market partners to improve systems, reduce bugs, and elevate the customer experience, while leveraging automation, agents, and our own AI technology to transform how support operates at scale. This Toronto-based role is currently remote and is expected to transition to an in-office arrangement. In this role, you will: - Own advertiser cases from initial intake through resolution, including complex or sensitive Ads Trust & Safety escalations; investigate whether issues stem from policy, review operations, product behavior, tooling, or another dependency, then communicate clear next steps and follow through. - Develop deep expertise across advertiser workflows, ads policies, enforcement processes, review systems, and support tooling. - Build a detailed view of advertiser friction by combining ticket themes, escalation patterns, quality findings, and service metrics to prioritize improvements and identify emerging experience or safety gaps. - Turn frontline learnings into clearer help content, stronger playbooks, better routing and escalation criteria, improved knowledge management and quality standards, and self-service opportunities. - Partner with Product, Policy, Engineering, Legal, Data Science, and Go To Market teams to resolve recurring issues, surface advertiser feedback, and scale durable solutions. - Drive operational excellence through AI-assisted workflows and automation that reduce manual effort, improve team efficiency, and elevate support quality. - Support readiness for new ads formats, features, and markets by anticipating advertiser questions and identifying support risks early. - Providing occasional holiday and weekend support on call coverage, as needed, to support business and customer needs. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have 6+ years of experience in customer support, user operations, ads operations, Trust & Safety, risk operations, escalations, or a related field, including ownership of high-impact customer or advertiser cases. - Bring strong investigative judgment and can translate ambiguous signals into policy support, operational gaps, product defects, and expected behavior - Can synthesize data trends, feedback, QA findings, and service metrics into clear priorities and system improvement while maintaining strong judgment and safeguards - Have improved support processes, knowledge bases, escalation workflows, routing systems, or quality programs. - Are comfortable using AI and emerging technologies (i.e. Codex, ChatGPT, OpenAI API, etc.) and/or code (e.g. Python) to automate repetitive tasks and integrating tools - Build trust with cross-functional partners, communicate clearly and empathetically with advertisers and internal teams, and drive action without formal authority. - Thrive in ambiguity, learn quickly, manage competing priorities, and bring a humble, service-oriented mindset. - Understand advertiser workflows, ads ecosystems, policy enforcement, account reviews, or ads safety operations. items.description: About Glean: Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles. At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level. Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality. If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more - deeply embedded where people get things done. You’ll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company. About the Role: Glean is seeking a talented security-focused software engineer to join our growing team. items.title: Director, Litigation
items.description: Perplexity AI is looking for a sharp, entrepreneurial litigation attorney to join our small legal team to help advance the business, protect the products we are building, and revolutionize the way people search and interact with the internet. This unique role offers significant responsibility, direct ownership of high stakes matters, and growth potential across an in-house practice group. This is a unique role within a rapidly growing AI technology company. You will play a key role in safeguarding Perplexity’s interests by managing litigation files and pre-litigation disputes related to our AI answer engine, models, and technologies, while helping to build and scale our litigation function. You will oversee complex disputes in a fast-moving and often unsettled legal landscape, spanning intellectual property (including copyright), privacy, commercial, and regulatory matters, and you will work closely with our AI, engineering, and product teams to assess legal risk, develop litigation strategy, and provide guidance during disputes involving our products and services. The ideal candidate combines deep substantive knowledge of litigation practice and procedure with strong business judgment and practical problem-solving abilities. You are comfortable confronting novel legal issues, including questions where the rules are still being written, and you bring intellectual curiosity about AI technology, adaptability in an emerging landscape, and exceptional collaboration skills. Success in this role requires a deep understanding of high-growth startup environments, where you will pair traditional legal expertise with sharp business risk assessment. We are seeking someone who is inquisitive, has an entrepreneurial drive, and the agility to thrive in our fast-paced environment. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES - Manage litigation matters and pre-litigation disputes across all phases, including strategy, pleadings, motions, discovery, depositions, hearings, trials, and appeals, while developing comprehensive case strategies that align with business objectives. - Provide counsel across a broad range of disputes, including intellectual property (copyright, trademark, and trade secret), privacy, commercial, and regulatory matters, in both first-party and third-party contexts. - Evaluate and respond to litigation threats, demands, and disputes across jurisdictions, developing appropriate matter-resolution proposals that resolve issues with minimal disruption to the business. - Select, onboard, manage, and collaborate with outside counsel across all stages of disputes. Negotiate budgets and fee arrangements, monitor performance, and hold outside counsel accountable for delivering optimal results while maintaining cost efficiency. - Partner closely with AI, product, and engineering teams to proactively identify litigation risks in product development and go-to-market strategies, and to collect information efficiently in support of active matters. Translate complex legal requirements into practical, actionable guidance for technical teams. - Assist in responding to regulatory investigations and inquiries from government regulators and private organizations relating to our products and services. - Build internal litigation processes, policies, and tools, including legal-hold and discovery workflows, that support litigation and regulatory matters efficiently and can scale with company growth. - Monitor the evolving legal and regulatory landscape for AI, copyright, and privacy; translate court decisions, agency guidance, and legislative developments into timely, executive-ready advice; and communicate with business leaders about ongoing litigation, emerging risks, and preventive measures. QUALIFICATIONS - JD and in good standing with an active US state bar membership (California preferred) - At least 15+ years of law firm and/or in-house experience handling complex commercial litigation (with experience representing emerging technology companies preferred) - Deep substantive knowledge of litigation practice and procedure, with a demonstrated history of strong outcomes and effective case execution - Exceptional analytical, organizational, and collaboration skills, strong business acumen, and the ability to partner with business and technical teams - An ability to communicate clearly and credibly with business and technical audiences, including translating genuinely unsettled legal doctrine into concise, business-relevant advice for executives and engineers without over-hedging - Hands-on attitude to tackle projects large and small, and a low-ego, roll-up-your-sleeves approach to working across the organization - Excellent composure in stressful situations, high level of integrity, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to work independently with limited guidance while exercising good judgment about when to escalate - Thrive working in a fast-paced, dynamic environment NICE TO HAVE - Experience managing copyright and privacy litigation, as well as commercial disputes, for AI or other emerging technology companies - Experience managing regulatory responses or investigations, including both first-party and third-party responses - Experience building or scaling a litigation function at a growth-stage company, with creativity and an openness to novel solutions - Experience litigating cases in multiple jurisdictions, including internationally - A passion for supporting the development of AI that is both innovative and trustworthy

items.title: Strategic Deals Lead, Cloud Compute
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As a Strategic Deals Lead, you will help shape Anthropic's long-term approach to AI infrastructure, compute capacity, and strategic ecosystem partnerships, and you will originate, structure, negotiate, and close the deals that put that strategy into effect. Within Cloud Compute, you will build and manage Anthropic's relationships across the emerging compute ecosystem to identify and execute opportunities that expand access to the infrastructure required to train and serve frontier AI systems. The compute market is fast-moving and structurally complex. Providers vary widely in scale, financial structure, and commercial model, and increasingly involve a variety of strategic partners. In this role, you will build and develop expertise across the relevant ecosystem players, commercial constructs and market standards, and the interplay between infrastructure and financing for scaling compute. You will work closely with Anthropic's technical infrastructure, finance, and legal teams to source and evaluate opportunities, develop deal economics, structure financing, and ensure transactions align with Anthropic's compute strategy. We are looking for someone with prior relevant transaction experience who is comfortable building and executing on a broad, active pipeline independently from day one. Key responsibilities Build and manage a pipeline of capacity across the integrated compute ecosystem Maintain and own executive level relationships with commercial, finance, and legal counterparts at providers across all stages of maturity Lead the full deal lifecycle for capacity agreements, from initial engagement and relationship development through negotiation, structure, and close of transactions Bring capital markets and finance expertise to transactions, developing frameworks for evaluating deal economics, counterparty risk, and the financing components of compute infrastructure Partner with infrastructure and technical teams to translate compute requirements into commercial terms and long-term supply strategies across the provider ecosystem Develop and maintain deep market intelligence on the emerging cloud and integrated compute landscape, including provider positioning, pricing dynamics, commercial model evolution, and the competitive dynamics shaping capacity access Represent Anthropic externally with corporate executives, investment banks, and infrastructure investors involved in transactions Drive internal alignment on transaction terms, risk parameters, and strategic priorities for Anthropic's compute supply Minimum qualifications Background in investment banking, private equity, or infrastructure investing, with direct experience in data center, cloud, or technology sector transactions Personal track record of originating, structuring, and closing cloud capacity, data center, or infrastructure transactions as the commercial, financing, or investing principal Deep familiarity with the compute ecosystem, including fluency in how different types of providers price and contract, how capacity commitments are structured, and how the integrated compute market operates Working understanding of the financing and infrastructure requirements of compute infrastructure projects Preferred qualifications 8-10+ years of experience in investment banking, infrastructure investing, or principal finance roles with ownership of cloud, data center, or compute transactions Experience managing multiple high-value transactions simultaneously at different stages of maturity and commercial development Demonstrated ability to build and maintain senior-level relationships with counterparts at commercially sophisticated, capital-intensive organizations Strong financial modeling skills, including the ability to build and pressure-test economics for large infrastructure projects Comfort operating in fast-moving, ambiguous environments where market structures, provider economics, and deal norms are still evolving A genuine interest in the trajectory of AI infrastructure and in Anthropic's mission of building safe, beneficial AI The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $265,000 — $325,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, Multimodal)
items.description: We are hiring builders to define how people talk to, show things to, and hear from AI In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. We've scaled beyond the millions of people using Perplexity every day for research, shopping, investing and curiosity into a new paradigm of using AI to transform knowledge into action. The Multimodal team builds the experiences and infrastructure that move AI interaction beyond touch and text — realtime voice, vision, and the platform systems behind them. We own the full path from a user speaking into a device to an answer coming back: the realtime session infrastructure that connects clients to frontier audio models, the backend orchestration that routes, records, and supervises live sessions, and the SDK that powers voice and multimodal experiences across Perplexity's apps. As a backend engineer on Multimodal, you will design and scale the distributed systems that carry live voice sessions in production — and drive entirely new products at the intersection of voice, vision, and agents. WHY PERPLEXITY IS DIFFERENT - Craftsmanship. We build high quality, tasteful products targeting both the AI native and AI curious. - Ownership. You identify the problem, design the solution and ship it. - Entrepreneurship. We think like founders, act with urgency, and hustle to deliver for each other and our users. - Scholarship. Work among highly talented peers, pursuing knowledge and truth, upleveling ourselves, our teams, and our products. - Partnership. We amplify each others' strengths, break down silos, and give selflessly to help our colleagues deliver excellence. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Design, build, and scale the backend session-worker architecture that powers realtime voice: durable per-session workers, provider routing, and stateful streaming over gRPC. - Own distributed-systems problems end-to-end — session lifecycle, crash recovery, reconnection and replay, multi-region deployment, and graceful degradation under real production load. - Build provider-agnostic streaming protocols from our backend to the Rust SDK that powers voice across every client stack. - Drive new products and initiatives in voice and multimodal AI from problem definition through technical design, implementation, and launch. - Build the orchestration layer that lets live voice models delegate work to tools, agents, and long-running tasks — safely, asynchronously, and at scale. - Partner closely with SDK, client, infrastructure, and model teams; work across the stack when the product demands it, from backend services to client-facing APIs. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 4+ years of professional software engineering experience building backend or distributed systems. - Strong experience in Rust, Python, or Go (we work primarily in Rust and Python). - Experience designing and operating production distributed systems: streaming RPC (gRPC or similar), stateful services, message-driven architectures, and failure recovery. - Solid understanding of cloud infrastructure — deploying, scaling, and operating services on AWS or equivalent. - Strong product judgment and the ability to translate user problems into simple, effective technical solutions. - Genuine interest and adoption of AI products and willingness to learn quickly. NICE TO HAVE - Experience with realtime media systems: voice, audio streaming, WebRTC, or low-latency transport. - Full-stack range — comfort building end-to-end, from backend services through client SDKs or web frontends. - Experience integrating LLMs, speech models, or computer vision into production systems. - Experience with agent frameworks, tool-calling architectures, or sandboxed execution environments. - Time spent at a fast-growing startup or on a high-ownership engineering team. OUR MISSION Perplexity’s mission is to power curiosity. Curious people are the people who drive change in the world. Driving change is a continuous cycle of learning, building, and integrating. Learn: curious people constantly learn new things by asking more. They question the status quo in their own expertise and they constantly learn outside of it.
